name: Lombard
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Lombard, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Lombard, IL: Jingle Bell Jubilee, the Lilacia Park lights with free Santa nights, Victorian Cottage tours and the Holly Jolly Trolley.
lede: Lombard builds its Christmas around Lilacia Park, the old Plum estate a short walk from the Metra station. Jingle Bell Jubilee lights the park in early December, and the lights then glow every night into January, with free Santa visits, Victorian Cottage tours and a Santa trolley.
celebrates: Christmas in Lombard centers on Lilacia Park in the middle of downtown. In early December the Lombard Park District and the Village of Lombard hold Jingle Bell Jubilee with more than a dozen partners. Helen Plum Library opens with a photo booth and snow princesses, the Lombard Historical Society hosts a Victorian Christmas with crafts and cottage tours, churches serve cookies, cider and concerts, and a free trolley links the stops before the park lights up and Santa arrives. The Holiday Lights then shine nightly into January, with free Santa visits on December evenings, and the park district's Holly Jolly Trolley carries kids from Mrs. Claus's workshop to Santa at the Log Cabin.
lastyear: In 2025, Jingle Bell Jubilee was planned for Saturday, December 6, with the Lilacia Park tree lighting at 5:30 pm. The Lombard Historical Society planned Gingerbread Way, a small holiday market with glow items and cotton candy, along with a gingerbread house contest, kids' crafts, face painting and free Victorian Cottage tours with costumed interpreters. Park board minutes from December 16, 2025, show the lighting ceremony went ahead: the parks superintendent thanked the marketing team for drone footage of it, and commissioners praised the partners behind Holiday Lights and the Holly Jolly Trolley.
facts: Lilacia Park began as the home of Colonel William Plum and his wife, Helen. Plum picked Lombard because the train ride to Chicago took about 30 minutes, and he bought a house on a hill near the station. His will left the land to Lombard as a park and the house as a free library in Helen's memory, and in 1927 voters created the Lombard Park District. Jens Jensen designed the park. In 2024, park crews put up about 900,000 holiday lights, and staff served 160 gallons of hot chocolate on the first night of Jingle Bell Jubilee.
trains: Lombard's Metra station sits at 20 S. Main St. on the Union Pacific West line, and Metra lists Lilacia Park as a 2 minute walk, about 0.1 miles, from the station, so the Holiday Lights make an easy train outing. The railroad shaped Lombard early: William Plum settled here in the late 1860s because the ride to his Chicago law practice took about half an hour. During Jingle Bell Jubilee a complimentary trolley links the downtown stops. For a bigger trip, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union and the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin run holiday rides.
train_links: The largest railway museum in the US, in Union, with a Christmas train.
Antique trolleys on a 1.9 mile line from 1896, plus Santa's Trolley Express.
traditions: Downtown Lombard's community-wide holiday evening ends with the Lilacia Park tree lighting and Santa's arrival.
Light shows, decorated trees and a gingerbread house glow in Lilacia Park every night through the holidays.
The Lombard Historical Society decorates its Victorian Cottage Museum for Christmas and leads tours, with a costumed docent on family tour days.
Kids make crafts with Mrs. Claus, then ride a decorated trolley to the Log Cabin to meet Santa.
Jingles the reindeer lends his name to a contest where families vote for the best lit-up homes using a park district map.
The Lombard Fire Department collects new toys during Jingle Bell Jubilee for Teen Parent Connection and Toy Express.
kidfact: Lilacia Park's lilac collection started with just two bushes that Colonel and Helen Plum bought at a famous garden in Nancy, France. Today the same park glows with holiday lights every winter.
faq: What is Jingle Bell Jubilee in Lombard?

It is Lombard's community-wide holiday evening on a Saturday in early December, run by the Lombard Park District and the Village of Lombard with local partners. Activities fill Helen Plum Library, the Lombard Historical Society, churches and shops downtown, a complimentary trolley links the stops, and the night centers on the Lilacia Park tree lighting and Santa's arrival.

Yes. The Lombard Historical Society lists admission as free, and Discover DuPage lists the event as free. Some stops sell treats, such as the Calvary Church Cookie Walk, where families pick homemade cookies and pay by the half pound, and the Candy Cane Lane market on Park Avenue has food and shopping.
Where are the best Christmas lights in Lombard?

Lilacia Park at 150 S. Park Ave. The Lombard Park District lights the park every night through the holidays from 4:30 to 10 pm with light shows, decorated trees and a gingerbread house, and Discover DuPage lists the display as free. The park district also posts a map of homes in Jingles' Holiday House Decorating Contest.
Can we take the train to Lilacia Park?

Yes. Lombard's Metra station at 20 S. Main St. is on the Union Pacific West line, and Metra lists Lilacia Park as a 2 minute walk, about 0.1 miles, from the station. That makes the park lights an easy evening trip by train from Chicago or the western suburbs.
Where can kids meet Santa in Lombard?

Santa makes free visits in Lilacia Park on several December evenings during Holiday Lights and arrives at the park for Jingle Bell Jubilee. The park district's Holly Jolly Trolley takes kids to meet him at the Log Cabin, and Yorktown Center hosts photos with Santa in its Center Court, with photo packages for sale.
Why is Lilacia Park so special?

It was the estate of Colonel William Plum and his wife, Helen, who brought back lilacs from France. Plum left the land to Lombard as a park, Jens Jensen designed it, and Metra notes it was named to the National Register of Historic Places in 2019. In winter it becomes the home of Lombard's holiday lights.
